title: Schuss Mountain Trail Map
new_html:
Welcome to one of Michigan’s top ski destinations—where terrain, trails, and fun come together at Schuss Mountain, Shanty Creek Resort.

Trail Overview
Schuss Mountain has about 42 trails for every skill level, plus 2 terrain parks and 7 lifts. All downhill skiing at Shanty Creek is at Schuss Mountain (Summit Mountain is home to Alpine Tubing).

Trail Difficulty
● Green Circle – Easiest: wide, gentle slopes for beginners
■ Blue Square – More Difficult: for developing skiers
◆ Black Diamond – Most Difficult: steeper, faster terrain

Lifts

  • Quad chairlifts – color-named (Red, Yellow, Purple and more) serving the front face and north side
  • Magic carpet and handle tow – for beginners, ski school and the Low Rider park

Terrain Parks

  • Mellow Yellow – the main park, with big boxes, rails and jumps
  • Low Rider – smaller features near the Yellow Lift, served by a handle tow; great for building confidence

Key Areas

  • Schuss Village – Base area with day lodge, rentals, tickets, ski school, and food
  • Cedar River Village – Lodging at the top of the mountain
  • Ski Patrol – On the mountain for safety and assistance

2026–27 Season (projected): Dec 5, 2026 – Mar 22, 2027
Hours: Sun 9am–4:30pm; Mon–Tue 10am–4:30pm; Wed–Sat and holidays 9am–9pm once night skiing begins.

Tips for Visitors

  • Start your day early for fresh corduroy runs
  • Green trails near the base are best for families and beginners
  • Use lift maps and signage to plan your route across the mountain
  • Helmets are recommended for all riders

Download full trail map: Schuss Mountain Trail Map PDF

title: Nordic Trail Map
new_html:
Explore the snow-covered beauty of Shanty Creek Resort through its scenic Nordic ski and snowshoe trails—about 9.5 km of groomed, track-set trails. Whether you're a beginner or an experienced skier, these trails offer a peaceful and invigorating way to enjoy winter.

Trail Overview (2026 trail map)
Pine Cone – 4.5 km (Schuss Mountain Village)
Winter Brook – 1.5 km (Schuss Mountain Village)
Arnie’s Way – 1 km (Summit Village)

Plus a 3 km groomed multi-purpose trail at Schuss Village for snowshoeing and fat tire biking.

Each trail is marked with difficulty symbols and trailhead signage. You’ll pass landmarks like Riverview, Red Lift Corner, and #3 Tee.

Nordic Center Hours

title: Cross Country Skiing
new_html:
Few activities showcase the beauty of northern Michigan quite like cross country skiing. Shanty Creek’s 9.5 km of groomed, track-set trails crisscross the resort’s villages to create a “village-to-village” experience whose benefits include staying warm in winter, a heart-healthy cardio workout, and a beautiful setting. This trail helps ensure skiers and bikers avoid accidents and unforeseen trail damage.

title: Alpine Tubing
new_html:
If skiing and snowboarding aren’t your thing—don’t worry! There’s still a fast and fun way to enjoy the snow. Alpine Tubing at Summit Mountain is a must-try winter activity, delivering all the thrills of sledding without the uphill climb.

You’ll hear laughter echoing across the slopes as guests of all ages race down the tubing lanes and ride the surface lift right back to the top. No skills required—just hold on and enjoy the ride!

🎯 What to Know:

  • Available Friday evenings, Saturdays, Sundays & holidays
  • Sessions start at the top of every hour
  • $30/hour
  • Online booking only
  • Participants must be 36″ tall

💡 Parents Note:
The last two hours on Friday and Saturday nights are recommended for Adults Only—ideal for grown-ups looking to enjoy some child-free fun.

Whether you're with friends, family, or flying solo, Alpine Tubing offers a unique and laughter-filled way to enjoy Shanty Creek’s winter wonderland.

More info & booking: https://www.shantycreek.com/ski/more-on-the-snow/

title: Grass River Nature Area Tours
new_html:
Kayak Tours

There is no better way to experience Grass River than by paddling its calm waters and enjoying its unique wildlife! On these guided tours, visitors explore Grass River by kayak and learn about GRNA’s conservation efforts, wetland plants, and wildlife. Adults and teens only.

  • Public tours run through summer and fall—see the Classes and Programs page on the website.
  • Private kayak tours for groups of 4–6: $50 per person including kayak rental; email james@grassriver.org.
  • Kayak rentals (June–September, reserve ahead): 231-533-8576.

Guided River Walks

Have a group that would like a private 2-hour tour led by one of GRNA’s knowledgeable naturalists? Walk the boardwalks over the wetlands to the river while a guide shares the history, conservation efforts, and local flora and fauna of GRNA. $100 minimum per group; allow at least two weeks’ notice. Contact james@grassriver.org.

title: Northaire Resort & Pontoon Rentals (Captained Options Available)
new_html:
Website: https://www.northaireresort.com

Phone: (231) 377‑7764

Resort & main dock: 7067 Crystal Springs Rd, Bellaire, MI 49615 (on Clam Lake)

Dock locations: Northaire has private docks on Torch Lake, Clam Lake, and in Bellaire. Confirm your dock location before heading out.

Experience northern Michigan’s shimmering Chain of Lakes with ease and comfort. Northaire has the largest pontoon rental fleet on the Chain of Lakes, with amenities like Bluetooth stereo, GPS depth finder, changing room, tow bar for tubing, ladder, and bimini top. Begin your journey on Clam Lake, cruise to the famous sandbar on Torch Lake, and explore scenic coves and the Grass River. Jet skis are also available at the Torch Lake location.

FAQs

  • Captain provided? Pontoons are self-drive. For a captained outing, book Northaire’s 2-hour Sunset Cruise.
  • Is alcohol allowed? Bring a cooler with drinks and snacks (please enjoy responsibly).
  • Pick-up and return? Pick-up starts at 9am and boats return by 7pm; staff contact you the night before to set your pick-up time.
  • Boating license needed? Michigan requires a boater safety certificate for operators born after June 30, 1996.

Tips

  • Arrive a little early for check-in and orientation.
  • Bring sunscreen, snacks, and a favorite playlist.
  • Tubes, lily pads, and porta-potties can be rented at each location.
  • The Grass River is a no-wake zone; stay toward the center to avoid shallow spots.

title: Lake Bellaire
new_html:
Just 1.5 Miles to Lake Bellaire

Discover this local treasure—a peaceful, scenic lake perfect for fishing, paddling, wildlife viewing, or a lakeside picnic.

• Fisherman’s Paradise (DNR Access): Developed boat ramp, dock, parking, and pit-toilet restrooms. A Michigan Recreation Passport is required; posted launch/parking fees (about $11–12) may also apply. Michigan Water Trails

Feel free to ask for help with maps, kayak or boat rental options, or the best times to fish!

title: Torch Lake
new_html:
📍 Torch Lake Info (Tip of the Mitt Watershed Council)

Just a short drive from your stay, Torch Lake offers legendary turquoise waters and world-class fishing opportunities. From casting for bass and perch in shallow bays to trolling deep for lake trout or salmon, this lake is an angler’s dream.

• What You Can Catch: Trout, bass, pike, salmon, perch & more
• Best Spots: Drop-offs, rocky points, and deeper waters
• Access Points: Torch Lake Township Day Park, Torch River Bridge DNR launch
• Need Help? Local fishing charters are available for guided adventures

Fishing Highlights

Torch Lake is a premier destination for fishing enthusiasts of all levels:

  • Lake Trout – thrive in the cold, deep waters.
  • Atlantic Salmon, Steelhead & Brown Trout – targeted by local trolling charters.
  • Smallmouth Bass – plentiful along rocky points and weed beds.
  • Northern Pike & Muskellunge – trophy-sized catches possible.
  • Yellow Perch – jumbo perch school up in the fall; great for families.

For guided fishing trips, check out local charters such as:

  • Charters North – Captain Shaun (231-590-1949)
  • Fish With Jim Outfitters (248-252-1277)

title: Clam Lake
new_html:
Website: https://watershedcouncil.org/waterbody/clam-lake/
Location: Between Torch Lake and Lake Bellaire

A long, slender connecting lake on the Chain of Lakes, Clam Lake offers good fishing for panfish, perch, and bass. The Grass River flows in from Lake Bellaire at the east end—a popular fishing spot—and the short Clam River carries the water out to Torch Lake. Because it’s smaller and calmer than the big lakes, it’s ideal for kayaks and smaller boats.

title: Grass River Natural Area
new_html:
Website: https://www.grassriver.org/

Phone: Office: 231-533-8314 • Center: 231-533-8576

Location: 6500 Alden Hwy, Bellaire, MI 49615

Hours: Trails open daily, dawn to dusk. Grass River Center: May–October daily 10am–4pm; November–April Sat–Sun 10am–4pm.

A 1,502-acre preserve featuring seven miles of trails, including 1.5 miles of accessible trails and boardwalk over fens and cedar wetlands. Ideal for hiking, birdwatching, observing wildlife, and educational programs at the nature center. Immerse yourself in wetlands teeming with otters, birds, and native plants—an excellent spot for families and nature lovers. Note: dogs are allowed on-leash only on the Rail Trail and Algonquin Trail, not on the boardwalks.

title: Glacial Hills Pathway & Natural Area
new_html:
Website: https://glacialhillstrails.org/
Contact: glacialhillspathway@gmail.com
Location: Just outside Bellaire; trailheads include Eckhardt and Vandermark (3 trailheads in all)

About 765 acres and 31.5 miles of trails for hiking, mountain biking, running, and winter sports, among old-growth forest and glacial hills. Routes range from the flat 1.5-mile Pine Tree novice trail to the 20.3-mile Outer Loop. Dogs are welcome on leash; no motorized vehicles or horses. Great for active travelers—stunning scenery and great trail variety.

title: Richardi Park (Intermediate River)
new_html:
Website: https://bellairemichigan.com/richardi/
Phone: Village of Bellaire offices, 231-533-8213
Location: On the Intermediate River just north of downtown; parking off E. Antrim St., Bellaire, MI 49615

Description: Features a swimming beach, carry-in access for kayaks and canoes, a large pavilion and gazebo (rentable), new playground equipment, tennis and basketball courts, and picnic space—all within walking distance of downtown Bellaire. In winter, the village builds ice rinks when conditions permit.

Why Guests Will Love It: Ideal for a fun family day—swim, paddle, picnic, or enjoy the playground. Great access to town amenities if guests want a snack or cold drink.

title: Craven Park & Campground
new_html:
Website: https://bellairemichigan.com/craven/
Phone: Village of Bellaire offices, 231-533-8213
Location: 3907 S Derenzy Rd, about a mile east of downtown Bellaire (enter at the end of E. Broad St where it meets S. Derenzy/Fairground Rd; map apps may give wrong directions)
